quest.title: Special Training
quest.description: Skirk agrees to help investigate the mysterious person's whereabouts. In the meantime, you should work on improving your strength.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

talks.objective: Begin the first round of special training

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ready?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, bring it on!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Your training will be split into three stages, testing your bladework, elemental abilities, and reasoning skills.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: We'll start with bladework. You're no rookie in this area, so I won't bore you with the basics.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: During your long journey, you've no doubt sparred with a lot of talented sword fighters. Consciously or not, you have picked up all kinds of techniques from them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet! There's Kaeya, Master Jean, Keqing... Oh, and Kazuha, Ayaka... Yeah, we've met sword masters like you in every nation we've been through.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sparred with a bunch of them too, right? Nice to know it's all gonna come in handy now!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Don't get too smug. In sword fighting, techniques alone are not enough — you need a cohesive system to bring it all together. A "style," or "school" of fighting.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: To use the human body as an analogy, your style is your skeleton — the foundation, the framework. Techniques are the muscles and other flesh attached to the bones. This is where your strength comes from.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Improving your sword fighting is like growing that body. If your frame got bigger and taller but you didn't add any muscle mass, you'd be weak and flimsy. Then again, if you packed on pounds of flesh without a big enough frame to support it, you'd end up bloated and unwieldy.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You need to do some introspection. Take a good, hard look at your past experiences, and figure out which parts of what you've learned are just techniques, and which parts can be used to form your own system of bladework.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Only then will you get the full utility out of all your thoughts and observations along the way. Only then will every strike you deliver make perfect sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, is that it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon thought you were gonna teach {NICKNAME} some cool new moves... Like when you went "swoosh" and opened a tunnel to another place!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: One day, you'll reach a new level of power where you realize that even that's as basic a trick as any other. But right now, our sword styles are so wildly different that teaching you mere techniques is pointless.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: There are no shortcuts in the pursuit of power. Failure is your best teacher, and rigor is your coursework.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That's all I have to say. Time to make a start — train until you're satisfied with yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Amazing... This is transforming my whole view of sword work. I'm using the same techniques as ever, but now they're having different effects.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's as if I've unlocked a hidden door in my mind, and there's a wellspring of strength on the other side.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (In my mind's eye, I'm seeing images of the friends I've made in Teyvat. Theirs are the sword styles and techniques I have come to know...)

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: "This moment will be frozen in time."

dialogues.speaker: Keqing
dialogues.text: "Cut to the chase!"

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Consider a moment of true mastery that you've witnessed in another person, and ask yourself — what lies beneath the surface? What's their guiding philosophy, what's their state of mind as they maneuver their weapon?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Now take that, and practice it right away with speed, skill, and strength... Over and over, until your hand is one with your mind. This is the only path to true growth.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: "Step on up!"

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: "Dance with the waves!"

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: "I see eternity go by in an instant, the autumns of many years from a single leaf. Thus I shall slice this maple in a flash, and ask a question of the ages..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (My sword style... My journey...)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: If you start to tire, empty your mind but do not stop.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Stay in that frame of mind as you keep up the fight. Get rid of all redundant movements. Imagine your sword is an extension of your own body. Wield it just as you wield your arms, hands, and fingers.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: "'Twas on a deserted moonlit night that the hero approached the vile dragon's limpid lair... Raincutter!"

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: "Feathers fleeting wet, the white heron treads water, a sight without flaw. Master of Inazuma Kamisato Art Tachi Jutsu..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (With each slash of my blade, I feel my strength increasing... I don't know if my weapon can contain all this power...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm in the zone. Limitless power is surging through me...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You slash and swipe till you've exhausted every ounce of your energy...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Huh... Looks like you've made some real progress. That concludes your training session.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Paimon knew you could do it!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: How do you feel?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: As you should be. Time flies when you're training hard. You've actually been going for several days now with no rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, meanwhile Paimon's had a whole bunch of naps! But you were so focused, she didn't wanna interrupt you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Go get some sleep — I'll be doing the same very soon. Let's hope you see that foggy place in your dream, so I can get this investigation over and done with.

choices.text: I'm fighting to keep my eyes open...

talks.objective: Go to the makeshift camp and rest
Go to the makeshift camp and rest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What is this place?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Have I been pulled back into that place again? But Skirk said the dream-mirroring would kick in when I fall asleep... so why am I back here?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...No, on closer inspection, this isn't the same dream as last time. It's dark and gloomy, but there isn't that chilling fog that made my hairs stand on end.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Hold on, if dream-mirroring is a two-way process... Maybe I'm seeing inside her mind while she's exploring mine?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If this is her inner world, it's pretty bleak... I can occasionally make out the sound of a flowing stream, but other than that... it's so empty.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What's that?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What a strange-looking creature — where did it come from? ...I think it wants me to follow it. Might as well see where it leads.)

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Skirk, why are you skipping classes again? We've talked about this!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Cause he's a crabby old man, and he's a boring old man! I don't like going to his classes!

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Excuse me!? You shouldn't talk about your teacher like that, it's very disrespectful!

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: Alright, let's not get into a big fight about this. Skirk's learned what she needs. There's no point forcing her to sit through more classes if she doesn't want to be there.

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: But I'd still love to hear about what you got up to yesterday. Why don't you tell your dad all about it?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I went diving! And I saw this huuuge fish. I never knew they could get that big! It looked kinda dumb though, with that stupid big fat head. I tried to shake its fin, but it just spat water at me.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Oh, and today, I'm gonna go to that prairie up north! There's supposed to be this giant bird there that can spit fire! I bet, if I climbed on its back, it could fly me all the way to the stars!

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: Hahaha, then I suppose your old dad should get one as a pet too. Otherwise, how are you gonna hear me call you for dinner up there in the stars?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: When it's time to eat, I'll come back on my own, silly... Anyway, gotta go! Bye, Mom! Bye, Dad!

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Wait... Put on a coat, at least! You'll catch a cold! I'm talking to you, young lady!

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: You spoil that child, you know. Ever since that merchant ship arrived, she practically lives outside. Always going on about "exploring the beyond one day," whatever that means.

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: Ah, let the kid do what makes her happy. Besides, we both know you're all bark and no bite. C'mon, our little adventurer's gonna be hungry when she gets back. Let's get started on dinner.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: ("The stars shimmer high above"... But, what lies beyond the stars?)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: (Mountains as far as the eye can see? An endless snowy plain? Or, maybe buildings taller than the sky, like the people from the merchant ship said.)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: (I can't be the only one asking these questions — the universe is fascinating. If only I could meet some other people like me, we could set sail together and explore every corner of the world!)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: (I'm sick of being a kid... There's so many amazing things out there, and I'm ready to see them all!)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: (But, for now... I'm starving. Better get back.)

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: Help...

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: Don't let a single one of them get away!

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: They're coming!

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: Don't be scared— Aaah!

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: Eliminate the threat.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Fire... There's fire everywhere! What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: I told you we shouldn't have trusted these "outsiders"!

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: Why are you doing this? What did we do to deserve this?

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: We welcomed you with our finest food and drink, showed you the best our home has to offer, gifted you cloth dyed by our own hands... And this is how you treat us?

dialogues.speaker: Panicked Passerby
dialogues.text: Run! Save yourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: Captain, zone three is clear and we have zone two surrounded.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: Begin extermination. Remember the orders from upper command — no one is to be left alive.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: Rest assured, sir. We have enough munitions to annihilate these savages and burn their entire civilization to the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: Good. The only ones who put up a real fight are that man and his wife, correct? What's their status?

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: We shot the man in the ankles, and the wife broke her wrist attempting to fight back. They won't be doing much more fighting. They're holed up in their home for now, but they won't last long.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: To prevent them from making some kind of last stand, we're planning to clear out the other zones first so we can send a bigger squadron to surround them.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: Well, well. Turns out some of these beasts do know how to use their claws. Now, the "threat" these savages pose will be undeniable.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: Let them cling to what's left of their lives for a little longer. Once the other zones are cleared, I'll cut off their heads myself.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Dad...? Mom...?

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Skirk! You're alright! Thank heavens...

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: So happy to see you, sweet girl. But, you need to go... It isn't safe here. They'll be back any second...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: What happened? You're bleeding a lot! Dad... Mom... *whimper*

dialogues.speaker: Callous Soldier
dialogues.text: Hehe, this is the place. Alert all units. Prepare to surround.

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Run, Skirk! Run as far away as you can! Don't trust anyone!

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: Your dad and I, we're not afraid to stare death in the face. But, we need you to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Strict Female Voice
dialogues.text: My clever girl, so curious... You're already so brave. I know you're going to grow up to be such a positive light in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: Whenever you miss us, just play this song.

dialogues.speaker: Cheerful Male Voice
dialogues.text: Remember... Life is a gift. Don't let darkness claim it.

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: Break down the door! Look what we have here. A savage that can pluck a tune! Well, the show's over!

dialogues.speaker: Callous Officer
dialogues.text: You! Stop singing! Shut it! I said shut it, or I'll make you! Fine, have it your way...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What was that...)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ah, you're awake.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I found a few clues while you were asleep, but it's only a start. Now, time for the second stage of your training.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: This time, the focus is elemental energy. Come find me when you're ready to begin.

talks.objective: Begin the second round of special training

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, staying in the Abyss feels so surreal, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No day, and no night — it's like time hardly exists. If we weren't careful to keep track, it feels like we'd have no idea how long we've even been here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, except for the fact that Paimon still gets hungry like clockwork... You go do your training. Paimon's gonna grab a bite.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready to start.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The way I see it, the pursuit of power is divided into three stages.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The first is mastering the use of standard weapons. Next is learning how to harness natural energy. And, after that, you're free to challenge even higher dimensions.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The "natural energy" of Teyvat is, of course, elemental energy. But that's not my area of expertise — I draw from a different source of power.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Abyssal power, yes. Also known as the power of the Void Realm.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: My master, Surtalogi, is a true expert in that area. After all, he was one of the group of five that infamously stole the all-encompassing power of the Abyss, an act for which the people of Khaenri'ah gave them the epithet "The Five Sinners."

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: The elemental energy of Teyvat, on the other hand, is derived from the power of the Light Realm. These two forms of energy exist in direct opposition to each other. Suffice to say, there's not much I can teach you this time.

choices.text: But, there's something familiar about the power you use.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #A keen observation, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Call it... respecting local norms. The Abyss stands in direct conflict with the will of this world. So, to make my life easier, I disguise my power to make it appear Cryo-like in nature.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It's a technique I learned from some Khaenri'ahn ruins, known as "the Seven-Shifting Serpent." If you ever change your mind about delving into Abyssal power, I can teach it to you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: So I've heard. You seem to have a knack for removing Abyssal power.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But... Is "purification" really what's going on there? Like I said — power does not simply disappear.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you trying to say?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...Just thinking out loud. Let's focus on your elemental training. That's what's gonna help us if the situation gets tricky.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: True growth comes from adversity. But only if you make the choice to pick yourself up again every time you fall.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: So, it's time to push yourself to the limit — and then keep pushing. This is the only way to advance at pace.

choices.text: I have the ability to purify Abyssal power.
It almost seems related to Cryo in some way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Along my journey, I've gained different elemental abilities in different lands.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... I've never trained them all at once like this.)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You need to understand what makes you special.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The ability to wield elemental energy without a Vision and switch between the elements at will...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: It means your aspirations need no approval from the gods. Your power is not bound by the rules of this world.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: So, be bold. Do not be afraid to chart your own path.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Graceful as the wind. Tough as stone. Nimble as lightning. Flourishing like foliage...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I can feel the power of the elements flowing through me. Sometimes, as peaceful as a flowing stream. Other times, surging like a raging river.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I close my eyes, I can almost hear their voices. But, it's not like some wild beast battling me for dominion. It's more like... saying hello to an old friend.)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Very good. It seems you've reached a deeper level of connection with the elements.

choices.text: How long has it been this time?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Long enough for you to lose yourself in your training — which is a good sign. Relentless practice with the elements has drained all your strength, but it's also what allowed you to make progress.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Get some rest. When you wake up, we'll proceed to the final stage of your training.

talks.objective: Go to the makeshift camp and rest
Go to the makeshift camp and rest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This place again...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (No response. The strange creature just floated away.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What is that thing? What is it doing in Skirk's inner world? And... where is it taking me this time?)

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: What is the secret to power?

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Longing? Hatred? Self-preservation? No... It is fear.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: The fear of losing those you love. The fear of watching your home burn. Fear of loneliness, fear of death...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Fear is the source of evolution — it forces humanity to adapt to their environment and overcome hardship. It is in the process of prevailing over our fears that we surpassed first ourselves and then the rest of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: That fear is now part of you. It calls on you to evolve, and it is time to answer.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Any minute spent missing home is a minute wasted — practice your sword work instead. Do not make me tell you twice.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: But, Master... I can barely lift the sword anymore. If I keep going, I feel like my wrist is going to break...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: So, it has not broken yet?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Then, pick up your sword and keep practicing until it breaks — I want to hear the cracking and splintering of bone.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: After all, bones can always be reset.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ugh... Aaargh...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Good, Skirk. Once again, you survived. How do you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Cold... In pain...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: These are signs that you are adapting to the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Each time the flesh is torn and the spirit crushed, each time you claw back from the brink of death, you become stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: I now understand why these people sought to destroy your homeland. Your potential goes beyond even what I could have anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: But, you still have much to learn in your pursuit of strength. Your mind is rife with distractions. From now on, I shall show no mercy in your training.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You must learn to shut out all the pointless emotion, crush the self that makes you weak, and become master over your physical form.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Get up, Skirk. Wipe the blood off your face, cut away the rotten parts of your flesh, and mend what is broken. Then, take up your sword.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: *coughing*... Yes, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The dream is over, but I can't get that suffocating, oppressive feeling out of my head.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I have so many questions about Skirk's past... Where does she come from? What has she been through?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're up! Hopefully, you got some good rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Skirk said to tell you that she's ready to start the final stage of your training whenever you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, wanna head over now? Or, did you wanna wait a little?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I really want answers, but right now it's vital that I complete my training...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Once that's done, I'll find a chance to talk to her.)

talks.objective: Begin the third round of special training

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: From your training so far, you have gained a better command of the sword and more control over your elemental abilities.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That's only part of it. Experience is the real teacher. Your journey, the friends you have made, the dangers you have faced — these have taught you more than I ever could.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Now, it's time to focus on how you react under pressure. You must be able to think rationally, even in unpredictable combat situations. To simulate this, I'm going to attack, and you're going to block.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Ready?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Hm, not bad. That defensive stance looks near unbreakable.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #Just like your {M#sister}{F#brother}. Ah, that reminds me. You still don't know what happened to {M#her}{F#him}, do you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, no fair! That's cheating!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You think every opponent has the same moral code as you? You can denounce their deplorable methods all you want... But, only if you live to tell the tale. The dead don't get to complain.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Strong emotions will always arise in combat — anxiety, anger, fear — but a true warrior is never at their whim. Only when you are free from the influence of emotion can you make the right choice no matter the situation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you describing yourself?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: How amusing. Almost sounds like you think you know me.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...But, you don't. You can choose your own path — we are not the same.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Let's begin. Try to use reason over emotion. Make the most rational and advantageous decision in any given moment.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: This is your final training session. Look alive.

choices.text: It's all thanks to your guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's not easy to control my emotions.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The battle is overwhelming, but... if I can just focus all of my attention on what my opponent is doing and how I should respond, it's almost like my emotions take a back seat.)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You're getting the hang of it.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The first step to controlling your emotions is controlling your mind. You want a unified train of thought. It all comes down to focus.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Focus... Focus on the battle...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I think it's working... I can choose to tune out anything that isn't relevant to the battle. But, I think I'm still pretty far from having full control over my emotions.)

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Your mind is rife with distractions. From now on, I shall show no mercy in your training.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You must learn to shut out all the pointless emotion, crush the self that makes you weak, and become master over your physical form.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Skirk went through this kind of training too, didn't she... How merciless does the training have to be to make someone substitute all emotion for pure reason?)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Stop. Let's pause here. One look, and I can tell your mind has wandered.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: That's to be expected. There's a limit to how long a human being can concentrate on one thing. Staying calm and focused sounds simple in theory, but in practice, it's more demanding than sword work or elemental abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Skirk is right. Now that I've stopped, all the emotions I was suppressing are rushing back to the surface.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Pain, exhaustion, frustration, doubt... But, exhaustion is the main one. I feel like I could fall asleep on the spot...)

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Get some rest — no point training further if you're already dead on your feet. Like I said at the beginning, the only goal of this training is for you to reach a point that you're satisfied with.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You managed to push past your limits, which is a good start. You can be proud of that and sleep well knowing that you've earned it.

talks.objective: Go to the makeshift camp and rest
Go to the makeshift camp and rest

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like I'm back in Skirk's inner world.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I don't see that strange creature this time. But, I think I can navigate this space on my own now, even without it here to guide me.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I don't know how to leave, so I'm stuck here until I wake up. Can't hurt to take a look around while I wait...)

dialogues.speaker: Steadfast Disciple
dialogues.text: Skirk is amazing! She faced down that terrifying giant and cut its head clean off!

dialogues.speaker: Bright Disciple
dialogues.text: She got hurt though, didn't she? I heard it was pretty bad...

dialogues.speaker: Steadfast Disciple
dialogues.text: Yeah, well that's a given. But the moment she was on the mend, she got right back to practicing her sword work.

dialogues.speaker: Steadfast Disciple
dialogues.text: I heard Master suffered a grave injury once too. Lost an arm and a leg, and still came back stronger than ever... Skirk's becoming more like him by the day.

dialogues.speaker: Bright Disciple
dialogues.text: Incredible... I wonder if I'll ever reach their level. They're always so resolute, so unshakable...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: *panting*

dialogues.speaker: Bewitching Voice
dialogues.text: Pathetic... You're not even trying. You're so much weaker than you think.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk's Mother's Voice
dialogues.text: Skirk, have you become a positive light in this world?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: *panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Bewitching Voice
dialogues.text: Do you even remember how many of us perished in that fire? How many bodies were left to rot on the scorched earth? Yet, you alone live on.

dialogues.speaker: Bewitching Voice
dialogues.text: Keep your gaze fixed on your blade. You don't deserve to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk's Voice
dialogues.text: I have so many questions! I just wanna jump in a spaceship, explore the whole universe, and get answers from the stars! I just need to wait till I'm grown up... Then, I can do anything...

dialogues.speaker: Bewitching Voice
dialogues.text: Now, you must bid farewell to who you were in the past, and become someone stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk's Father's Voice
dialogues.text: Run, Skirk... Run! Only death awaits us here. Keep running, and don't ever look back...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: *panting*... *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let's see here. First things first, you need a new identity.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Going around telling people you're from somewhere beyond the stars won't do, now will it? How about saying you hail from "beneath the earth" instead?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: As the Khaenri'ahn saying goes: "Venturing out into the universe and down into the abyss are the same in that both are braving the dark unknown."

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Well, I'm a visitor on this planet, so I'll follow the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, splendid! That saves me quite a bit of trouble. Let me offer you a piece of advice in return — although it might not be what you want to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I know the pursuit of strength is important to you. But, taking a moment for yourself every once in a while is never a bad idea.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ignore "her" existence for too long, and there will come a day when you can no longer hear "her" voice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The dream is over. I can hear the crackling of a fire in the distance, and there's a fragrant aroma in the air... Mmm, grilled meat...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're awake!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You must be starving, right? Ta-da! A barbecue feast just for you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, of course you are! That's why Skirk and Paimon got this all ready for you. Dig in, before it gets cold!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, well, if you're around someone long enough, it's bound to happen. Plus, Skirk can cook! So, Paimon decided she can forgive the whole "ice queen" thing. Paimon's not one to hold a grudge...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Here's an idea. Let's save the chit-chat until after the meal.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You all dig in and make quick work of the food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oof... So full...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, it's Paimon's turn to sleep now. Wake her up when it's time to go!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I have good news.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: First, your training is complete — you have what it takes to wield immense power, now it's just a matter of putting it into practice. Continue to learn from your journey and hone your skills against formidable opponents.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Second, I've located the culprit we've been searching for. Next, we just need to retrieve the missing part of your soul, and our business will be concluded.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: When Ajax trained with me, he once told me he was "bursting with questions." So, I allowed him to ask me three of them before he left.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #You and I may never meet again, {NICKNAME}. So if there's anything you want to ask me, now's your opportunity. Just like Ajax, I'll answer three of your questions.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (After spending time in Skirk's inner world and witnessing her memories, there are so many questions I could ask. But, the most important one is...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you... really from Teyvat?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...Okay, not the angle I was expecting. What makes you ask that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sorry I didn't tell you earlier, but... while we were dream-mirroring, I think I saw your memories.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is the first time I've seen Skirk break her composure. I guess this really took her by surprise.)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I knew that was a possible side-effect... Closed off my mind to you for that exact reason.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Even with the dream-mirroring, you should have seen nothing but endless darkness.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So, Skirk didn't share those memories with me on purpose. And in fact, she tried her best to keep them from me.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, speaking of endless darkness... On my first time there, that was all I saw — until that strange creature appeared...)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Eh, whatever. Must have been a flaw in my execution... I shouldn't be too surprised. Due to some recent circumstances, my self-control has been lacking as of late.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Since you've seen what you've seen, there's no reason to hide the truth. All I ask is that you keep it a secret.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No, I'm not from Teyvat. I'm from a different planet, and there was a time when I journeyed through the stars — a lot like you, in some ways.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Like me? Do you mean... you're also a Descender?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No, we're different in that respect. You're influencing the fate of this world, but me? I'm just passing through.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Several hundred years ago, my master, Surtalogi, opened the border between worlds and sent me here.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But, this is not my home, and one day, I'll return to the vast unknown of space... So, there you have it. Onto your second question.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is your goal in coming here?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To become stronger.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: For certain reasons, I need to bridge the power gap between me and my master as quickly as possible. But, first, I need to understand the source of his strength.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To do that, I need to follow in his footsteps, walk the path he once walked. And somewhere along the way, I'll find out how to defeat him. That is my sole focus and purpose.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...Okay, you have one question remaining.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk's goal is to defeat "The Foul"? I can hear how serious this is for her. I wonder what those "certain reasons" could be...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But, given how quickly she blazed through that answer, I doubt she wants to talk about it. I have one question left. What should I ask?)

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: You make it sound so easy. Ever since the incident I experienced there, I've never stopped searching for Master Skirk and that unknown abyss.

response.speaker: Childe
response.text: But it's been years now and I've still found nothing...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh... Maybe I should take this opportunity to get Childe some answers.)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Well? Your last question?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know Childe is looking for you, right? Are you going to let him see you?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Ajax...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: His situation is different than yours. Before you ever crossed paths with me, you'd already encountered many formidable people, studied their techniques, and developed your own skillset.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: So, during your training, all I had to do was build upon that foundation. But, Ajax was so young when he came to me — a complete blank canvas.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Children can't help but imitate their role models. In the long run, that would only hinder his growth.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Once Ajax has enough strength in his own right, I will allow us to meet again. Until then, let that motivate him to reach his full potential.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That was a calm and calculated answer. It's like she was talking about something entirely mundane... I don't know why, but I'm not buying it...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She makes it sound like the decision has everything to do with Childe and nothing to do with her. But, what does she actually feel about it?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Abyss is completely silent. This domain must get lonely after a while. Not to mention, she said it's been hundreds of years since she arrived in Teyvat — and even longer than that if you account for how slowly time passes in here.)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Unlike you, I have no desire to establish a connection with the world. The weak and the lowly have no right to remember me. They're lucky they only have a few missing memories to show for it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (In all that time, she never established a connection with this world. Was it really just because she looks down on the weak?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...I doubt she'd give me a straight answer if I asked. Besides, I already used up my three questions. She was happy to give me cold, hard facts. But, I still feel like I haven't heard her true "voice.")

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Wake up your companion. It's time to go.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Oh, and everything I just told you... Best keep it a secret from her as well.

choices.text: That was a lot faster than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Sometimes, you have to practice a single movement a million, maybe ten million times, before the breakthrough moment comes. Nothing in the outside world can help you in this process — the most important thing is to remain patient.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: If you wish to master the elements at a fundamental level, you must see the entire natural world — nature in all its places and forms. That is part of what it means to be a traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Warriors will train day and night to perfect their skills, but when the battle comes, their fate may be decided in a matter of seconds.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: One mistake, one moment of hesitation, and just like that, all their blood, sweat, and tears were for nothing. You need to push yourself to perfection, or you might not even live to regret it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You train the elemental powers one by one, ending with Hydro...
